Subject: Redwood renewal — draft order form + a couple of clarifications

Jasmine / team —

Thanks for sending the draft MSA + order form last week. We ran it past procurement and legal this morning and have a compact set of redlines focused on: (1) the capacity lanes in Exhibit B, (2) a term alignment (18 -> 24 months), and (3) a short-stay clause for pilot credit carryover.

Attached is our annotated order form (Statholdings_Renewal_OrderForm_redlines_v1.docx). High-level asks:
- Can you confirm Redwood is ok with the proposed 24-month term? We want the pricing protection for the longer window.
- Exhibit B: we consolidated burst capacity and baseline into two lanes; need confirmation on how that maps to Dedicated vs Hosted routing in the platform.
- Audit/evidence: procurement asked for an evidence package that shows retention and SLA measurements for the prior 6 months.

We want to keep this tight — target signing in the next 10 business days. Can you triage and flag any items that will need legal Ops escalation?

Thanks,
Tom Hayes
VP Procurement, Statholdings

Tom —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the clear asks. Quick read-through, and then we'll do a triage flow:

1) Term length: Sales is fine with 24 months from a commercial standpoint — we will confirm pricing brackets with finance and return a simple term amendment if required.
2) Exhibit B lanes: tagging @Neha and @Laura — the way Statholdings collapses burst into a secondary lane will affect how we map routing policies (Hosted fallback vs Dedicated reserved). We need a brief ops note on: a) how committed baseline converts into Dedicated capacity; b) how burst is billed if routed to Hosted.
3) Evidence package: we can produce a 6-month SLA/evidence zip but will need ops to pull cost & retention metrics.

I'm attaching the customer's redline doc (as received) and a quick checklist. Proposed next steps:
- Internal triage with Legal (Laura) and Renewals (Neha) today.
- I’ll push a clean counter with track changes (MSA + Exhibit B) by Friday EOD.

Questions for you before we move the redline: do you require a specific indemnity carveout for the pilot workload? Also can procurement confirm the signer and DocuSign path (single-signer vs two-signature)?

Best,

Hi Jasmine —

Thanks for triaging so quickly and for the evidence package. A couple of clarifications from legal:

1) Term / Price protection: Statholdings will accept 24 months provided we get explicit price protection language in the order form (we've highlighted proposed text in the attached markup).
2) Exhibit B mapping: we do want the burst lane to be expressively capped and billed at a different rate when routed to Hosted. Please include an explicit fallback billing rule that states how burst is invoiced when Served by Hosted vs Dedicated.
3) Indemnity / pilot carveout: we are ok with the standard Redwood indemnity language but request a limited warranty paragraph for the pilot workload (3-month acceptance window) — we've annotated the MSA.

For signer path: Procurement prefers a two-step: 1) Signed by Redwood rep via DocuSign (single-signer), 2) Counter-signed by Statholdings procurement. If you can send a DocuSign envelope with the two-step flow we can route internally.

We attached a redline PDF with highlighted clauses (Statholdings_Renewal_OrderForm_redlines_v1.docx -> exported). We can make one final pass after your counter.

Best,
Alice Moreno
Senior Counsel, Statholdings
